claim: A perfect AI system could fully automate reconstruction and cut the cost of a mouse brain connectome by at least tenfold
quote: A hypothetical perfect AI system could lead to complete automation and thus reduce the overall cost of producing a mouse brain connectome by at least an order of magnitude

claim: Machine-learning limits put estimated manual labour for a mouse connectome in the billions of dollars
quote: limitations in machine-learning performance lead to estimates of manual labor costs in the billions of dollars

claim: Image segmentation is the rate-limiting computational problem for connectomic reconstruction
quote: The computational problem that is rate limiting for progress in connectomic reconstruction is image segmentation

claim: The most critical requirement is tracing axons and dendrites over centimetre lengths against nanometre voxels
quote: centimeters in the case of axons in a whole mouse brain, as compared to the million-fold-greater underlying voxel resolution

claim: A single segmentation error (premature axon termination or merged dendrites) causes multiple connectivity errors
quote: individual errors in the segmentation (such as prematurely terminating an axon or accidentally merging together two distinct dendrites) can cause multiple errors in the final

claim: In a recent petavoxel human connectomics project only about 0.001% of the data were labelled for training
quote: in one recent petavoxel-scale human connectomics project, roughly 0.001% of the data were labeled for training

claim: State-of-the-art tracing reaches error-free lengths of about one millimetre in some cases
quote: error-free lengths of one millimeter in some cases

claim: SAM applied to connectomics EM performs far below specialised neurite-tracing approaches
quote: its performance is far below specialized neurite-tracing approaches

claim: On CT and MRI segmentation SAM underperformed and was rescued only by extensive fine-tuning plus added architecture components
quote: rescued only by extensive fine-tuning (with specialized task-specific data) and additional model architecture components

claim: Synthetic text data has helped most where examples can be checked automatically, as in code or mathematics
quote: synthetic data have been especially helpful in situations in which examples can be automatically checked for relevance and correctness, such as code or mathematics

claim: No simulator yet produces data detailed enough to compare with connectomics volume EM
quote: Simulators that are capable of producing data with sufficient detail to be comparable to volume electron microscopy used in connectomics do not yet exist

claim: Biomedical synthetic image data have so far enriched real training data rather than replaced it
quote: such synthetic data have been useful largely as a means to enrich standard (that is, real) training data, rather than as a replacement for them

claim: Implausible generated microscopy samples could not obviously be filtered without a human expert
quote: it is unclear what criteria could be used to filter them out without the intervention of a human expert

claim: Using all available raw data in training is lower-hanging fruit than synthetic data
quote: a much lower hanging fruit than synthetic data is to use all available raw data when training segmentation models

claim: Self-supervised pretraining helped subcellular annotation and cell typing but has yet to affect connectomic segmentation
quote: have yet to make an impact on connectomic segmentation

claim: At exabyte scale, inference efficiency will be a primary factor in system design
quote: inference efficiency will be a primary factor in overall system design

claim: Applying large models to connectomics will probably require distilling them into smaller specialist models
quote: The application of large models to connectomic analysis will therefore probably require ‘distillation’

claim: Alternatively foundation models may complement specialists by mimicking human proofreading, using shape priors such as NeuroMorpho
quote: foundation models would essentially mimic the human proofreading that is currently required to complete connectomic reconstructions
